The Recorded Sayings of Master Yungu, when first residing at Shengshou Chan Temple in Pingjiang Prefecture, compiled by the student Zongjing.

The Master entered the temple on the eighth day of the eighth month in the fourth year of Baoyu. Pointing to the triple gate, he said: "There is the power to pull it open; one must possess the penetration [to enter]."
Open your eyes! Until now, none have been able to enter the Gate of Holy Longevity. Today, the new Elder lets you go.
*Shouts.* To the Buddha Hall: Do not seek it in the Buddha; do not seek it in the Dharma. What is the use of bowing? Holding up his sitting mat, he says: "To let this pass would be a grave error."
According to the tradition of "closing the room" (Makakashō), Vimalakīrti remained silent. [Zhaozhou] struck the meditation platform and said: "The Taihu Lake spans thirty-six thousand acres;
when the moon speaks from the heart of the waves, to whom does it speak?"
Holding up his robe: "At Mount Kukkutapāda, it was kept securely; at Mount Dayu, it could not be lifted. Holding up the Dharma robe, he said:
"As for this—'Is there anything I conceal from you? I conceal nothing from you.'"
Ascending the seat, he held up the incense and said:
"This one offering of incense is respectfully presented to prolong the sacred life of the present Emperor—ten thousand years, ten thousand years, ten thousand times ten thousand years!
He then took his seat and delivered this introductory remark: "Ten thousand acres of misty waves; wind and moon across four bridges; a thousand-foot line cast straight down."
Drooping down—three great mountain tortoises are lightly pulled by a single tug. Is there anyone who does not crave the fragrant bait? (The dialogue is not recorded). Grasping the main thread:
before the patterns have yet appeared, Suzhou is here and Changzhou is here. As soon as a hair’s breadth is revealed, the Main Mountain is high and the Foremountain is low.
Leaving no trace in any place, yet accomplishing everything in every place. Amidst the clamor of the red dust marketplace, they cast two and throw three.
Amidst the heaped white waves, they display their oars and dance with their paddles. From the Southern Chuihong to the Western Hepu, you people come and go;
you people nod your heads in agreement. Yet, consider this: when Baoshou opened the hall and Sansheng recommended a monk, Baoshou struck him immediately.
What is the intent? "Holding Mohe Panthe crosswise, I issue the true command; across the realm of Great Peace, I behead the dull and obstinate.

In the evening small *sīmān*, after the questions and answers were concluded, he said: "When Deshan held a small *sīmān* and did not answer questions, he displayed the majesty of Fulin splitting Mount Taihua.
When Zhaozhou held a small *sīmān* and required answers to questions, he exhibited the power of the Golden-Winged Bird cleaving the vast ocean. If it is thus..."
To mention one is to clarify the three; it is like weighing things on a scale with precision. It is like a magnet seeing iron: a light tug and it moves. What need is there to say "thirty blows"?
What need is there to say "throwing a brick to draw out a tile"? Tonight, there is no merit in movement, nor is there any contact with worldly customs.
The tracks are transformed yet the highway remains open; the oceanic course follows its own systematic order. Do you understand? Lake Tai spans three prefectures.
Again, Master Bao raised the matter of sending someone to deliver a message to Dashi: "Why do you not descend the mountain to teach and transform sentient beings?
Why do you merely gaze at the clouds and the Milky Way? Dashi replied, "The Buddhas of the three periods of time have been swallowed by me in a single gulp;

what sentient beings are there to transform? The Master [Zhaozhou] comments: "Of these two great elders, one has a sweet mouth but a bitter heart; the other, as soon as he is supported, [falls back]."
[Zhaozhou] was intoxicated. Within the gate of proclaiming the teaching, this is indeed so; however, if we speak from the standpoint of the patch-robed monks, one must simply be dripping with blood.
[He] struck the meditation pillar once and said: "A cart should not be pushed sideways; there is no principle for a crooked judgment."
Ascending the hall: Twenty days since entering the monastery, I have been in a state of constant flux, hurrying here and there. When meeting monks, I inquire deeply after their well-being;

when seeing laypeople, I bow low in greeting. Why is it that out of ten people, five pairs are found? Those who encounter such opportunities often miss the mark. Nevertheless, disaster does not enter the door of the prudent.
The Buddha ascended the hall for his final nirvana and said: "When birth-and-death have ceased, the cessation of cessation is bliss. Yellow-faced Gautama, having died, cannot be brought back to life.
He beat his breast and addressed the assembly; he displayed his twin-soled feet from within the coffin. Yellow-faced Gautama, having lived, cannot be brought back to death.
The Holy Life has a secret method of transmission: dying so as to live, and living so as to die. Thereupon, he took up his staff and struck the ground with it.
Suddenly he said, "Alive! Alive! Do you all see Old Gautama? He leaned on his staff and said, "Not it, not it.

[This was] the Hall Discourse given by Chief Seat Jing of Tiantai and Librarian Wang of Jingci, thanking [them for their presence]. In Jiangnan and Liangzhe, the spring is cold and the autumn [is mild].
"Hot! Clearly one speaks of it yet does not know it exists; clearly one knows it yet cannot attain it. After a long silence, he said:
"The great tiger that Fenggan rides is originally the white-browed beast of the South Mountain."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: A monk asked Fengxue, "When speech and silence involve transcendence and subtlety, how can one pass through them without transgression?
Fengxue replied, "I long remember the third month in Jiangnan; where the partridges cry, the hundred flowers are fragrant. The Master commented:
"The Yellow-Faced One from Zhejiang recites a divine mantra, binding all the people of the great earth with a single seal until they cannot even breathe."

It is so. Even the Sage’s life could not avoid reciting the *Pu-huixiang* (Universal Dedication) mantra. When one reaches the lands of Jiang and Wu, the rivers end and the mountains of Yue stretch across the opposite banks.
Engraved upon the "Square Pearls and Jades" (fangzhu yu), the True Dharma Eye of Vulture Peak and the Broken Sandpot of Mount Zhongfeng are upheld and sustained.
He rose, shook heaven and stirred earth, and gave a shout, saying: "I walk through the wild weeds; you, again, enter the deep village. He ascended the hall and said:
"The fire of the mind blazes fiercely; the wind of objects sweeps vast and wide.

To manifest the great capacity and great function of Deshan and Linji, and to shatter the seven perversions and eight inversions of sentient beings mired in worldly toil—do you understand? A house of skilled merchants does not stockpile dead goods."
Xie Wuwai ascends the hall for the first time on the seat: "A single leaf falls and the world turns autumn—how can you understand it this way?
A single mote of dust rises and the great earth is gathered in—how can you understand it otherwise? This 'this way' and 'not this way' are iron walls upon iron walls.
Nevertheless, were it not for one with clear eyes, it would be most difficult to fully comprehend."
Master Xie of Mount Jingshan ascends the hall with Attendant Hang of Wenzhou and Custodian Xiang. The entire Great Canon is like a *pātra* girl chewing frost and ice with her full mouth.
Having personally arrived at Cao Creek, he circles the bed while shaking his staff; he plants thorns upon level ground. He has raised it, and he has finished raising it;
he has picked it up, and he has finished picking it up. Do you understand? The monks of Sichuan are rugged and coarse; the monks of Zhejiang are elegant and refined.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: A monk asked Xianglin, "What is the matter beneath the patched robe? Xianglin replied, "In the twelfth month, fire burns the mountains.
The Master commented: "In the twelfth month, fire burns the mountains; his words are upright and his speech is likewise upright. The white clouds gather at the mouth of the valley."
The bright moon bathes the balustrades.

On the eighth day of the twelfth month, a great snowfall occurred. Master Yǎnxī of Jìngshān arrived. He ascended the hall and said: "Two thousand years ago, two thousand years after—how marvelous, how marvelous! How rare, how rare!
Whether emerging from the mountains or descending from them, it is all for the purpose of teaching and transforming sentient beings. Do not..."
"Is there anyone with eyes who has awakened to the heart of the matter? If not, I, Shengshou, shall add frost to the snow.
He struck the meditation pillar with his staff and descended from the seat.
On the first day of the New Year, he ascended the hall: "Today is the first day of the first month; in speaking, there are many taboos. If one speaks of the Buddha-dharma, others will say..."
If one speaks even a single word of the Buddha, one must rinse one's mouth for three days.

If one speaks of worldly matters, it is said that under the gate of the Patriarchs, vulgar talk is not permitted. Holding up his staff, he said, "Let this staff reveal a bit of news. He struck it once.
"A thousand head of oxen advance; a hundred steeds advance."
Ascending the hall on the Lantern Festival: The moon is full in the heavens; it is the half-moon among men. One lamp becomes hundreds of thousands of millions of lamps;
everywhere the radiance is brilliant and resplendent. Suddenly, mist gathers and clouds arise, and heaven and earth become pitch black.
Where is the lamp? After a long silence, he said: "I am reminded of Xianglin’s saying: 'Proving a tortoise to be a turtle.'"
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: A monk asked Yunmen, “The luminous, silent illumination pervades the sands of the Ganges.
Yunmen said, “Is this not the speech of the scholar Zhang Zhuo? The monk said, “It is. Yunmen said, “Your words have fallen. The Master commented:
“Before the spark of a flint, within the shadow of a flash of lightning—if you attempt to follow in their tracks, you will be a thousand miles, ten thousand miles away. Nevertheless, where is it?”
This monk fell into a trap of words. After a long silence, he said: "The path has no lost items; the gentleman praises this excellence. Ascending the hall, he said: "The spring days linger on;
the spring colors remain lingering. Seeing the peach blossoms, one no longer doubts; hearing the bamboo strike, one forgets all that was known.
Why is it that one person says they have not yet understood, while another says they have not yet reached the ultimate? After a long silence, he said: "A great forge of refinement."
Gold should not change its color.
[The Master] looked over the words of Fohai of Mount Jing and ascended the hall, saying:

"From the single transmission at Vulture Peak to the direct pointing at Shaolin, from the beginning at Shengyuan Pavilion to the end at Lingxiao Peak—within these two intervals, nothing has ever been spoken. Do you all know this?"
Where does the Buddha-ocean descend? Its patterns and colors have already been revealed.
[The Master] ascends the hall to thank the Librarian and the Vice-Abbot. As for the entire Tripitaka of the teachings, what kind of thing is it? It is like the morning sun, thin and pale.
These words cannot be interpreted by one who is a "sleeping tiger," nor can they be manifested by one who is merely a "seller of ginger. Its...
Other paths may attain it; black beans are good for making sauce, and white rice is good for making porridge. Yet the Holy Life is unwilling to nod its assent.
Why? Because his home is in the Western Capital.
Ascending the hall for the Summer Retreat, he took up his staff and struck it once.
"If you can grasp the meaning here, the assembly on Vulture Peak remains present and has not yet dispersed. If you cannot, then listen as this staff recites a verse on the summer retreat.
He struck it once again and said, "Too much flourish!"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Baizhang suffered Baizhang’s shout; Linji received Huangbo’s staff. Piercing the brain, stuck in the glue-pot; throwing oneself into the net of the law.
As for 'this side' and 'that side,' three hundred, five hundred—how vast their deliberations!
Is there still blood beneath the skin? He struck the meditation pillar once and said: "The iron whip has great strength; it only regrets having no enemy."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Members of the monastic community, possessing the eyes for traveling the path and manifesting the ultimate core, you wield the vajra mallet to shatter the nests of sages and ordinary beings;
you grasp the sword of wisdom to sever the life-root of Buddhas and patriarchs. The entire Tripitaka is but worn-out paper used to wipe away sores;
the seventeen hundred transmissions of the lamp are merely the idle furniture of a monkey’s play. He gave a shout.
It is not necessarily that a virtuous cause brings about an evil fruit.
Entering the hall [the Master said]: "Dharma’s wall-facing; Yunmen’s seven days of silence. Thunder crashing on dry land; the scorching sun in a blazing sky. The ancients were like this;
Shengshou is not like this. One blow leaves a scar; one slap leaves blood. It must be so."
What? For six months there was no heat; the five grains did not ripen.

Upon breaking the retreat, he ascended the hall: "Ten thousand miles, not an inch of grass; once you step out the door, it is all grass. A swift falcon soars into the void; a fierce tiger stands in the path.
He slaps the meditation seat and says: "Even an eye-opening monk cannot see through this."
On the Mid-Autumn Festival, the Master ascended the hall: "The two sides are dark, the lake is level, and clouds enshroud the green peaks.

One does not realize that the moon of the mind is solitary and full; often one greedily gazes at the heavens above. Have you all awakened with vigor? This is precisely the time for cultivation; this is precisely the time for making offerings."
The reconstruction of the Yuanzhao Hall and the formal address from the abbot’s seat: One zhang deep, one zhang wide—this is the model for Buddhas and patriarchs, the standard for all time.
Take, for instance, the Yuanzhao Hall; last night it vied with the Sangao Hall for precedence.
What rank does this represent? After a long silence, he said: "The eyes of the assembly cannot be deceived."
Opening the furnace, I ascend the hall. Facing the Holy Monk, I sit in meditation; to the earthen image, I preach the Dharma.

The embers of two thousand years ago have already been deeply stirred and fanned. Do you all feel your entire bodies breaking into a sweat? If not, then wait until they grow cold before applying them.
The Record of the Chan Monastery Benjue in Jiaxing Prefecture, compiled by the student Daojie.
[The Master] occupies the room, holds his staff horizontally across his chest, and says: "The true command is fully upheld—iron walls, iron walls! He strikes the ground once with the staff.
It is said: "Baizhang was deaf; Huangbo stuck out his tongue.
Taking up the notice: "The Treasury of the True Dharma Eye, entrusted at Vulture Peak, is precisely here today. What is the matter of today?"
This inscription was issued by Jiaxing Prefecture.
Entering the hall for discourse: "The phrase that cannot be uttered even with one’s full strength has been spoken three times in the hall;
it has also been spoken once at the striking of the bell. Hearing this being said, some bite off their thumbs; hearing this being said, others knit their brows.
The Eyebrows. Although it is thus, there is one gain and one loss.
[He] ascends the hall to express thanks to Venerable Long’an, as well as to Zhou the Inspector, Daming the West Hall Master, Xingsheng the Head Seat, and the Attendant.
"Zeng Shen once attained the 'Yes' (yi wei); Kāśyapa once broke into a smile. The calamity that consumes the plains begins with a single spark; as for carrying...
Muzhou’s board and the breaking of the sand basin are entirely like pouring oil to extinguish a fire, causing its flames to flare up even more. He lets out a shout and says:
"In broad daylight under a clear sky, how could such a thing exist?"

A letter from the late Master Jingsi Jishi arrived. He ascended the hall and said: "The law of impermanence and birth-and-death Is like the towering Southern Mountain leaning against the edge of heaven;
It has no concern with me. The shimmering West Lake soaks the moon in its cold clarity. I shall further speak a verse of 'Be Careful' (Zhēnzhòng)."
Eighty-nine, clearly distinct; seventy-two. Empty space forms two sides; where it is less, there is a void, and where it is more, there is an addition.
This is the Old Man of Stone Tablet giving a false confession for the dead. Today, at Shoushan, I shall overturn it entirely and bring it back to life. Do you understand?
If one were made to shed tears frequently, even the vast ocean would surely dry up.
Master Xie, the Librarian, ascends the hall. He cites a case: A monk asked Master Wuzu, "The entire Tripitaka is a 'cutting foot' (a radical).
I wonder what character it cuts? Wuzu replied, "Bolanang. The verse says: A single phrase fully presents the Sanskrit sutras;
The tongue reveals the sounds *dì*, *dū*, and *dīng*. One might not have known they were thought to be level tones, But upon arrival, they are found to be oblique.
仄平 (Zè píng). Ascending the hall: "To eliminate the phrase that is right; to eliminate the phrase that is wrong. This drives a rooster to hatch a swan's egg.
Thus it may be so; thus it may not be so. To let go of the dead snake and seize the live scorpion—this is what I originally sought to express. This is the intent.
Regarding this: The founding master Jinghui personally met the old man Longya.
He ascended the hall and cited the following: Master Ying’an asked Master Mian, “What is the Eye of the True Dharma?
Mian replied, “A broken sand pot. The Master commented: “The old man Mian, in front of the Hall of Great Penetration, turned the ‘only’ into a taboo name.”
Truly, the orthodox lineage has been swept from the earth. Do you all understand? Even kalpa-stones may wear away, but one’s native dialect is difficult to change.
On the anniversary of the Buddha’s Nirvana, he held up the incense and said: "I caught the wind [of his teaching] before the Peak of Taibai, where people speak with left-handed tongues;

I investigated further at the assembly on Vulture Peak, where the great thunder resounded through my ears. From that time on, resentment has coiled within my breast, and I have even sought to humiliate his school."
"Householder, Old Monk, I do not value your ability to untangle the sticky; I only value your ability to add further bonds. I do not approve of your total withdrawal;
I only approve of your total letting go. Burn this incense with such earnest devotion—this is called the true Dharma-offering."
Ascending the hall on New Year’s Day: Today I wish to speak of the Buddha-dharma of the new year, yet it has already been spoken by Jingqing.
I wish to speak of the phrase of non-transmigration, yet it has already been spoken by Fachang. Having no choice, I shall simply speak to you all based on the present moment.

Xie Lin’an ascends the hall for the sake of Administrative Officer Lin of Jing’an, Attendant Ying of Wangshou, Attendant Jian of Lingyin, and Abbot Jun of Shangtang.
Vimalakīrti’s single silence; National Teacher Huizhong’s three calls. The clouds gather in the azure sky; thunder roars through the great void.
But as for the entire Great Canon—does it still contain this news? *Pah!* Do not ask in the city of Chang’an.

At the Imperial Capital, the furnace was opened and the hall ascended. A single interpretation of this freezing cold: six years at Snowy Ridge, nine years at Mount Song—yet not even half was attained.
This mountain monk intends to practice it; yet, "exhausting the Dharma leaves no people. For now, let us simply blend with the light and share in the dust. Fire.
The house was warm. After a long while, he said, "How wide is the brazier compared to the width of an ancient mirror?
He ascended the hall and raised this case: While Yaoshan was sitting, a monk asked, "What are you brooding over so intently?
Yaoshan said, "I am brooding over that which cannot be brooded over. The monk asked, "How do you brood over that which cannot be brooded over? Yaoshan said, "It is not thinking."
Verse: Twisted ancient trees lean against the cold forest; Buried by snow and frost, the news of spring remains deep.
Suddenly, a gentle breeze lightly stirs them; Listen closely, and it is all the sound of this dragon’s roar.
Ascending the hall for the inauguration of the Imperial Birthday: A single phrase, free from partiality, is revealed in the open presence. Lightning encircles the polar star;
a rainbow flows over the Flowery Isle. Truly, throughout heaven and earth, all things sentient and insentient alike leap for joy.
Why is this? When the Sage acts, the myriad things behold.

[Huijue asked,] "Did you come by boat or by land? [Ju said,] "By boat. [Huijue asked,] "Where is the boat now? [Ju said,] "At the foot of the steps. [Huijue asked,] "How do you express the phrase that does not involve traversing the journey? Striking his sitting mat once, he said, "You fabricated old man! You are like hemp or millet! Then he shook out his sleeves and departed.
Langya asked an attendant, "Who was that? The attendant replied, "It was Master Ju. Langya then went in person to the guest hall and asked, "Was that not Master Ju?
Do not be offended by our slight encounter just now. Ju then let out a shout. Again...
Question: "Venerable sir, when did you arrive at Fenyang? He replied: "I arrived at such-and-such a time. Dongshan said:
"While I was in Zhejiang, I heard your name long ago. It turns out your understanding is only like this; how then can your reputation spread throughout the world?

Langya then prostrated himself, saying: "Huijue’s transgression! The Master [Yunmen] commented: "One man is like a dragon sporting in the vast ocean, causing the waters of the four seas to stand up in waves."
A man is like a tiger crouching at the foot of a cliff; ten thousand sounds arise with the wind. Master and guest are both complete; life and death are both complete.
Let us set aside the ancients for a moment—how then do master and guest encounter one another right now? *Aḥ!* If you understand this kind of matter, then simply rest.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Speaking from the mouth, every word flows toward the source; employing the pivot from the hand, every mechanism accords with its counterpart.
But as for Linji’s withdrawing his tongue for an eon and Deshan’s setting aside his staff—where do they meet? After a long silence, he said: 'Descend from the seat.'"
Circulating the hall for tea.
Ascending the hall, he held up his whisk and said: "If you can see it here, a single mote of dust flies and obscures the heavens;
a single mustard seed falls and covers the earth. If this is not yet so, the whisk passes through the lantern and enters the pillar, heading toward the eye of a gnat."
[The Master] turned his body around. "He has opened up the world! He threw down his whisk.
Entering the hall, he raised the following case: When Gaoting first visited Deshan, he inquired from across the river.
Deshan beckoned him with his hand, but Gaoting strode away crosswise without looking back. Later, he became a Dharma heir of Deshan. Dahui commented: "Gaoting..."
He hurried off crosswise. If one were to grant that he was a sharp-witted monk, it would not yet be enough for him to be a dharma heir of Deshan.
Why? Because he still has the Yangtze River between him and Deshan. Master Chijue said: "Deshan possesses the poison of a sand-crocodile that shoots at people;
once Gao-ting is dead, he will never live again. The Master [Wumen] comments: "Deshan possesses the skill of wielding a chisel..."
The hand possesses the quality of being shaped by the axe; at that time, it further received a meal of fish stew and thick broth from Lizhou.
The tradition of this lineage has not yet reached a state of desolation.
As for the words spoken thus by Master Dahui and Old Man Chijue—whether they are praise or blame, one knows the sturdy grass in a gale and recognizes the loyal minister in times of upheaval.
Ascending the hall at the commencement of the summer retreat: This ninety-day period begins this very morning. Everyone, take your time with your progress, yet act with urgency.
Suddenly you may come to know that the eyes are beneath the eyebrows and the nose is above the lips.
I permit you to know, but I do not permit you to see. Do you wish to see? [He reaches out his hand and touches his nose. How is it?
Xie Bingfu ascends the hall for the summer retreat. "A single phrase contains all flavors"—the Chief Administrator has brought this forth.

"A single phrase is bland and tasteless"—the Head Seat has brought this forth. It causes all of us in this assembly to suddenly cast off our hunger and emptiness, and for both hearing and seeing to vanish.
I, the mountain monk, also have one flavor; it is simply pungent and bitter, yet I wish for you all to swallow it.
He spat out his saliva. Holding up his staff, he said, "Today’s offering—how does it compare to yesterday's?
He ascended the hall. A monk asked Master Ma, "Beyond the four propositions and transcending the hundred negations, I ask the Master to point directly to the meaning of the Westward Transmission."
The Patriarch said, "I am weary today; I cannot explain it for you. Go ask Zhizang. Zhizang said, "I have a headache today;
I cannot explain it for you. Go ask my elder brother Hai. Elder Brother Hai said, "When I reach this point, I do not understand.
The monk reported this to Mazu. Mazu said, "Zang’s head is white; Hai’s head is black. The Master [Dongshan] took up this case.
It is said: "Poetry gives rise to it; ritual establishes it; music completes it. This is indeed so. But do you still know the point where he directly points to people?
After a long silence, he said: "The people may be made to follow, but they cannot be made to understand."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised this case: A monk asked Dongshan, “When cold and heat arrive, how can one avoid them?
Dongshan said, “Why not go to a place where there is no cold or heat to avoid them? The monk asked, “What is the place where there is no cold or heat?
Dongshan said, “When it is cold, it freezes you; when it is hot, it burns you. The Verse says: A new melody from Xinfeng, a song of the snowflakes; Clouds enshroud...
The ancient hall is deep and silent at night; throughout heaven and across the earth, there is no divergence.

Do not mistake the *shang* tone for the *yu* tone. Baomiao ascends the hall and cites: "National Teacher Nanyue Huairang said to Master Mazu, 'Your study of the Dharma-gate of the mind-ground is like sowing seeds.
My preaching of the essential Dharma is like the moisture from heaven. Because your conditions have converged, you shall see its [fruition].'"
The Master said: "Such talk as this is merely the matter of ordinary daily life. Driving the ox at Mount Mui, one plows through the clouds and sweeps away the moon;
wielding the hoe at Magu, one plants shallowly and digs deep. One removes the weeds of ignorance to nourish the sprouts of the numinous.
Would you call this the Dharma-gate of training the mind-ground? Is it like sowing seeds beneath the earth? One spreads the compassionate clouds densely and sprinkles the sweet dew everywhere."
The sun of wisdom is loftily suspended; the profound breeze blows uniquely. To call this "the essential Dharma I preach"—is it comparable to the celestial rain?
When the five grains ripen in abundance and the myriad treasures flourish with fruit, the entire household is sated at once, and all prior hunger is forgotten.
To call this "because of the convergence of conditions, you perceive the Way"—is that so? (He strikes the meditation seat once and says: "The Venerable Master of Jinzhou is laughed down!"
Xie Su, Xin'en Cheng, and Preacher Sheng, attendants, ascend the hall. Within the smile of Kāśyapa lies the ultimate meaning; beyond the diagrams of Fuxi is the transmitted teaching.
When the dragon and serpent obtain the clouds and rain, the falcons and hawks soar in the autumn sky.
Leaving the city to return and thank old friends, he ascends the hall. At the crossroads, turning one's head and looking back is simply for the sake of waiting for someone to come.
At the village path, pinching the tip of the nose—where has the wild duck ever flown away? If you can see it in this way, you have seen.
Meeting under a tilted canopy as if we were old friends.
Should this not yet be so, then from West Qin to East Lu, at the summer retreat’s conclusion, before the fifteenth day: stay, stay, yet there is nowhere to stay.
After the fifteenth day: go, go, yet there is nowhere to go. On the very fifteenth day itself: neither going nor staying. This is the dissolution within the Hall of Original Enlightenment.
Summer Retreat. A *pindapāta* dance within Nalanda Monastery.
On the anniversary of Chan Master Fohai’s passing, he ascends the hall: "A single leaf falls from the branch in the courtyard; the entire earth is imbued with autumn colors.
How lamentable are those who study the profound mystery—how few truly know the seasons! He slaps his knee and says: "When Zhaozhou met Nanquan that day, he was able to say..."
"Radishes grow in Zhenzhou.
[The Master] ascends the hall and cites a case: A monk asked Yunmen, "What is it like when the trees wither and the leaves fall? Yunmen said, "The golden wind reveals its essence.
The Master comments: "To respond to the season like the wind and to respond to the stimulus like lightning—Yunmen, the old man, was certainly not lacking in this regard."
Looking closely, it is truly a matter that wounds the sinews and moves the bones.

On the occasion of the Head Seat Daji’s ascent to the hall, he manifested great potential and displayed great function; piercing the target and breaking through the dust, he struck the mark with every shot.
He established the orthodox succession for ten thousand years and extinguished the true lineage of Dongshan. He has proven that the sheep he stole was originally in Chang.
The Hall Bell for the Corridor Bees.
On the first day of the ninth month, he ascended the hall and cited the verse by Ciming thanking his old friends: "Splashing and cool is the autumnal scene; Fellow men visit this desolate place.
Tea is brewed with water from beneath the mountain; The cauldron is heated by firewood from within the cave. Ciming was a man of great wealth... [text continues]
Prideful. To be restrained yet not frugal—nevertheless, this does not exempt one from using the permanent property of the monastery. Original Enlightenment is not like this:
amidst the rustling, cool scenery, companions visit a place of solitude. Arsenic mixed with wolfsbane, white rice sprinkled with fine pepper.
Now tell me, is this the same as the ancients, or is it different?
Ascending the hall on the Double Ninth: The golden wind whistles; the jade dew glistens. The purple [flowers] bestow their purple; the yellow chrysanthemums bestow their yellow.
Princes and nobles everywhere ascend heights to chant and admire. But as for the man of the Way beneath the forest trees, here he is with two or three companions, gathered together to deliberate.
Now tell me, what is it they are deliberating about? The ninth day of the ninth month is the Double Ninth Festival.

Ascending the hall, [Zhaozhou] raised up a triangular object and showed it to the assembly, saying, "If one discusses this matter, even the raising of a single eyebrow is already a missed opportunity.
Magu came forth from the assembly and said, "I do not ask about the missed opportunity; what is this matter? Zhaozhou said, "A missed opportunity."
Magu overturned the meditation seat; Sanjiao then struck him. Xuedou brought this up, saying: "These two fellows have heads but no tails.
Before their eyebrows have even blinked, how can you speak of 'missing the mark'? A monk then asked: "Why do the eyebrows not blink?
Xuedou struck him. The Master brought this up, saying: "These two great elders—one acts before the spark of a flint."
[The Master] clapped his hands. One person thrusts their shoulder forward within the shadow of a flash of lightning; it is a state of total release and total gathering, total life and total death.
Why did Xuedou say, "Two fellows with heads but no tails"? Those with eyes must discern this for themselves.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The cranial bone of Śākyamuni and the eyes of Bodhidharma are in the valley among the reeds, in the pit among the reeds.
He struck the meditation seat and said: "It is smashed to pieces! The scales are even; the ground is level."
On the arrival of the festival, he ascended the hall. The golden crow flies and the jade hare hastens; today is the day the first yang arises. Holding up his staff, he said:
"This coarse and pungent pear is black as lacquer all over. Is there growth here or not?
He then raised the staff and said: "Seven feet, eight feet."
Ascending the hall, he said: "A flash of lightning, a clap of thunder—cliffs collapse and rocks shatter. Too swift for ears to cover, too swift for eyes to blink.
Through the vast silence of a thousand ages, who knows this? When Huangbo heard it, he was so startled that his tongue lolled out."
The Buddha ascends the hall after attaining the Way. Before Mount Zhengjue stands the old monk who freezes to death yet does not die, who starves to death yet does not die.
When the time of Mingtan arrives, he cannot avoid deceiving himself and annotating for himself. *Tu!* The source of calamity resides here. In the human realm and the heavens above.
Master Xie Mingzang ascends the hall: "The nostrils of the Patriarchs and the fangs and claws of the predecessors—when realized, all things are of one house;
when not realized, there are ten thousand distinctions and a thousand differences. But as for the saying, 'The sutras return to the Canon and Chan returns to the Sea,' how do you understand this?
The flawless jade of Bian has yet a flaw."
Ascending the hall to pray for clear weather while circumambulating the streets, and simultaneously expressing gratitude to my old friends from the Jing Mountain Monastery:
that which is within stillness and that which is within clamor—if it is not, then it is entirely not; if it is, then it is entirely so. Panshan turned his back on the meat-stall;
Louzi attained enlightenment amidst the sound of singing. You all, who have been circumambulating the streets in procession these past days—do you not share the same path and the same tracks?
"Dimo! Aha! No guest stays overnight at the Dragon Gate; yet in the tiger’s den, a cubs is born. Ascending the hall, he raised this case:
"Mañjuśrī is the teacher of the seven Buddhas; why was he unable to emerge from the woman's samādhi?
What supernatural powers did Wǎngmíng possess that he could emerge from the woman's samādhi? The Master said: "Setting aside for a moment whether he emerged or did not emerge, tell me—"
Do you know where the World-Honored One’s vulnerability lies? The jade seal does not leave the hand of the Son of Heaven; how could the golden casket belong to a commoner?
Compiled by the practitioners Weining and Zonghui from the *Record of the Chan Master of Kaiyuan Temple in Jianning Prefecture*.
Occupying the hall, he held up his staff and struck it, saying, "To maintain the Dharma in this manner, all people throughout the world will surrender their doubts upon merely hearing its wind.
Leaning on the staff, he said, 'When you arrive, I shall not point.'"
Having ascended the seat, offered incense, and finished his prayers for the Emperor (the questions and answers are not recorded), he then said:

"The Buddhas do not appear in the world, yet the clarity is vivid—the bright moon shines in the vast sky. The Patriarchs did not come from the West, yet they stand solitary and remote—clouds arise in the deep valley.

Thus it is that the numinous sprouts flourish uniquely upon Mount Zizhi, and the splendor of light overflows at Danqing Pavilion. This is not merely within the jurisdiction of the seven provinces; it cannot be measured by the staff."
"Free from sorrow. It shall cause all people throughout the great earth to attain universal peace through effortless effort. Nevertheless, where does the ultimate merit reside?
After a long silence: "A thousand peaks pay homage to Mount Hua; ten thousand streams flow solemnly into the vast ocean."
Again, he cites the case of Master Mengbi of Jianzhou. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? He replied, "I will not comment for you.
The monk said, "Is this not it right now? He replied, "You are deceiving me. The Master composed a verse: "One phrase fully presented does not deceive you."
Where one intends to open the breast, one deceives oneself; gazing long at the moonlight, it blends with the clouds into white. Unawares, the sound of the spring carries the chill of the dew.
On the occasion of the Mid-Autumn Festival, he ascended the hall. A monk came forward and asked: "Today is the fifteenth of the eighth month; this is precisely when the full moon faces the door."
"Though it pervades the earth and fills the heavens, for now not even a thread or a hair is revealed. The Master said, "Sitting beneath a covered basin, how can you blame anyone else?
The student asked, "The candela pillar emits radiance; the lanterns all dance together. The Master said, "Do not yet wear your flower.
The student asked, "Facing the objects of perception, with whom can one speak of this mind? It makes one long remember the poet Hanshan. The Master said:
Hanshanzi said, "What does he say? Jin replied, "I recall that in the past there was an abbot who asked Mazu Daoshi, 'How is your venerable state these days?
Mazu said, 'The Buddha of the Sun’s Face, the Buddha of the Moon’s Face. The Master said, 'The Old Monk has vomited it out.'"
Jin said, "The sun-face and the moon-face are so suddenly manifest they are difficult to discern; a master with clear eyes sees them at once.
The Master said, "If you see the cheek behind the head, do not engage with him. Jin said, "But tell me, after seeing it, what is it like?
The Master said, "Sun-Face Buddha, Moon-Face Buddha. Jin said, "A gust of west wind comes, and two or three leaves fall. The Master said, "Is that so?"
"If you wish to see Master Ma, it will take sixty kalpas across three lifetimes. The student advanced and said, "The moon of mind is solitary and perfect; its light swallows the myriad phenomena.
The light does not illuminate objects, nor do objects exist [independently]. When both light and objects are forgotten, what is this? The Master said, "It cannot be traced and cannot be painted.
The student said, "Is it not that the moon is stamped upon the vast sky, and the river reflects its shadow? The Master said, "Precisely."

[The Master] said, "This is walking within light and shadow. The student asked, "At Vulture Peak, [the Buddha] spoke of Caoxi; when has anyone ever recognized their own nature? The Master said, "The moon?
The student said, "As soon as one conceives a thought, it is obscured by black clouds; even if one recognizes it, it is still not it."
The Master said, "It shatters the skull, yet you still do not awaken. The student asked, "Without recognition and without deliberation, what is this?
The Master said, "Prostrate yourself."
The Master raised [the case]. Hanshan said: "My mind is like the autumn moon; its light shines brightly upon the azure pool. There is nothing with which it can be compared;
how shall I be asked to describe it? [The Commentator] says: Since it cannot be described, let us cast one out from the mold:
"My mind, the autumn moon, stamps its seal in the midst of heaven; wherever it meets, it is everywhere perfect. Let us all go together to sit beneath the forest trees—how wonderful!"
Look before light and shadow have yet arisen.
[This was] the Dharma Hall discourse given by Master Xie and Monk Konggu. Taking up the alms bowl, he occupies the seat of Nanquan.
Who is the host? Who is the guest? How many years has the Elder practiced the Way? His wisdom surpasses that of the birds; having caught the bird, it is already prior to the time of Wei-yin.
Master Wang’s descendants are like rats, bobbing their heads in and out of a mousehole; what common ground for conversation could there be?
If you wish to illuminate the majestic style of the gate of great wisdom, you must first be deaf for three days. (He lets out a shout and says:
"I have traded my old sword that once slew the Luan-demon for a yellow ox to teach my descendants."
Ascending the hall on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month: Four times nine is thirty-six; sleeping at night is like lodging under the dew. Gautama was coldly deceived by the stars.
He stubbornly claims that all sentient beings are fully endowed with wisdom and virtuous marks. *Tut!* To speak of dreams while one's eyes are open!
Xie Nanjian invited Master Beishan Guangxiao of North Mountain to ascend the hall. He raised the following case:

Changqing said, "When one meets a fellow traveler on the road with shoulders touching, the task of a lifetime of study is finished. The Master commented: "Zishan and Nanshan have been fellow travelers on the Way for thirty years."
Throughout the eastern and western Zhejiang regions and across the mountains of the north and south, we have met many times and stood shoulder to shoulder on countless occasions;
yet, we never once spoke of the two characters "studying Zen. Why? Because both of us were aware of our own shame.
Ascending the hall for the Buddha-bath ceremony: When body, speech, and mind are pure, this is called the appearance of a Buddha in the world.

When the face is covered in dust and body, speech, and mind are impure, this is called the passing away of a Buddha. If you can clearly realize this while drenched head to toe in mud and water, no gratitude could ever repay such kindness.
If this is not yet the case, even if you exhaustively use the waters of Jianxi to wash yourself, you will never become clean. Why? Because water does not wash water.

Ascending the hall, he raised this case: When Master Changsha returned from traveling the mountains, the Head Seat asked him, "Where have you been? Changsha said, "I have been traveling the mountains. The Head Seat asked, "Where did you go? Changsha said, "At first I followed the fragrant grasses away; now I follow the falling blossoms back. The Head Seat said, "This is very much like the spirit of spring. Changsha said, "It is even better than autumn dew dripping on lotuses. Verse: The fragrance of the spring breeze fills the valley; The falling flowers drift upon the stream. If one can discern the meaning within these words, One will know that the ancient path is not far off. The moon shines over the green mountains; The clouds rest upon the white peaks. When the mind is free from both gain and loss, Then the true source is revealed. The head seat’s question was like a cold wind; Changsha’s answer was like a warm spring. If you can see through the words and phrases, You will realize the ancient road is right before you. The dew on the lotus fades with the passing night; The spring breeze brings life to the willows. If you can understand this in an instant, You will see that the Way is not hidden. Do not seek it in the ten directions; Do not look for it within yourself. If you can let go of all conceptualization, Then you will see the Buddha-nature clearly. The ancient sages have already spoken; Why do you still seek elsewhere? If you can grasp it in a single thought, Then you will know the ultimate truth. The head seat’s question was a test; Changsha’s answer was a response. It is said: A single step is taken, and another follows immediately; casually, one’s body stands by the Wuling Brook. Within the cave, there are boundless tidings of spring;
it is simply that people of the age have lost their way.
The Head Seat Xie Lingfeng Shiping did not attend the invitation from Longguang. He ascended the hall and said: [He] raised the case:

"Sansheng asked Xuefeng, 'What does the golden fish that has passed through the net eat? [and so forth]. He commented: "At the Dragon Gate, ten thousand fathoms high, only one such as he can pass through;
at Elephant Bone Ridge, with its thousand layers, reaching the summit requires a true master. Setting aside the ancients for a moment, what about today’s new Dragon?"
Guang met with Zhifeng. They conversed for some time about various matters, after which [Zhifeng] said: "On the path ahead, one's person is as light as a leaf;
yet one's lofty reputation shall weigh as heavy as a mountain for a thousand ages."
At Zhongxia, he ascended the hall: "Half the year has passed; half the summer retreat is over. At the Danqing Pavilion, walking east and west;
on the long benches, eating porridge and rice—everyone says this is a ready-made koan where nothing remains unaccomplished. But let me ask you:"
Why did Bodhidharma come to Liang? Why did Kāśyapa Mātanga enter Han? [A monk] asked.

The Master ascended the hall and said: "To speak of mind and nature, to cite the ancients and the present—this falls into the thicket of entangling vines. Only by grasping the essential meaning before the pivot of the occasion can one transcend."
Even one who unexpectedly clarifies the fundamental source still falls into the thicket of entanglements. Ultimately, how can one avoid this?
[He] throws down his staff and says:
"Be careful! Ascending the hall, [he said]: "The upward-moving faculty, the cliff-edge phrase—under the three-beam roof, silently contemplate and maintain it; on the ten-roads street..."
Magnificent and manifest! [He] lets out a shout. A swift falcon does not strike a dead rabbit.
Entering the hall for instruction, he raised the following case: Huangbo asked Master Baizhang, "How do the ancestral masters of yore instruct people?"
Baizhang sat down. Huangbo asked, "How will your descendants transmit this in future generations?
Baizhang said, "I thought you were a man of substance," and then returned to his quarters. The Master [Dongshan] commented:
"I have often heard that Baizhang’s family laws were rigorous and his gate was high and steep. Why then, upon Huangbo’s lightest prod, did the inner sanctum open wide? Although..."
Nevertheless, who among those of past and present has ever truly arrived?

Upon ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat (*varṣā*), one observes the practice of *śīla* and *samādhi* during the period of seclusion; it is like pressing down a cow’s head as it grazes. To fix a date for realization is to "strike the grass to startle the snake.
If you have sinews in your eyes and blood beneath your skin, the nest will be aware before the wind reaches the winnowing fan, and the *bi* star will [signal the end] before it has even risen.
When it rains, one knows the hollows. Throughout the vast expanse of all directions, as you step forward, what bowl are you seeking?
Entering the hall, he said: "The wind whistles, the rain whistles; every faculty corresponds, every thing is utterly transcendent. If you understand it thus,"
The twenty-fifth day of the eighth month. Should it not yet be so, you bag-carriers, open the furnace and ascend the hall.
Today we open the furnace; there is a saying: the fire tongs and the incense spoon are made entirely of iron.
Ascending the hall, he said: "To speak when silent; to be silent when speaking. Iron walls, layer upon layer; silver mountains, one after another.
Xuefeng went nine times, yet there was no door for him to enter. Linji thrice received a severe beating, yet it was not thorough. Why? Simply because it is too clear."
